Description: Gives an example of the file types processed by the text compiler.  Furthermore it shows how the macro expressions look like and how the table data is inserted into the text stream that is written to the output file.

This example extends the previous one by the use of multiple data tables, recursive macro processing, the use of multi line macros and the use of additional parameters from the command file to generate a C++ and a Visual Basic .NET data class.

This example shows a how to describe a state machine using a matrix. The matrix is used to generate a C++ state machine class. It is designed to derive another class from it that reacts to the state changes. The generated code is documented using doxygen style. Additionally a dot graph description is generated that causes doxygen to produce a graph of the states and transitions when it is run. The example folder contains a template to generate code for a console application for testing the state machine.

Shows how to integrate the text compiler into MPC (The Makefile, Project and Workspace Creator) files for creating projects containing text compiler command files. It consists of a batch script that creates the MPC files for the examples. Furthermore it runs the MPC workspace creator to create the example solution and projects.
Shows how to create a syntax highlighter definition file for PSPad editor using provided tables. This example can be used as basis for creating definition files for other editors.
The documentation of the code-creation-kit is created using it's text compiler.
